items.title: Context Language Models Explained!
items.summary: Context management is one of the biggest bottlenecks for AI agents. When the context window fills up, most harnesses compact or summarize the conversation and lose useful information along the way. Meta and the University of Washington's new paper, Context Language Models, lets the agent edit its own context like a file instead. The catch: it breaks your prefix caching. Full video, with my tests on a DGX Spark: https://youtu.be/Bgtr1Ue40Jo Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725 #AIagents #contextengineering #LLM #shorts

items.title: Grounded Generation, Hallucinations & LLM Evaluation: Assessing Model Output Quality
items.summary: AI can be confidently wrong. Here is why it happens, how grounding fixes it, and how to measure whether it worked. Terms covered: - Hallucination: models are trained to generate statistically likely text, not to verify facts. When a model does not know, it fills the gap with something plausible. - Grounded Generation: anchoring responses in verified, retrieved sources so answers are traceable and far less likely to be fabricated - LLM Evaluation: assessing outputs for accuracy, relevance, coherence, cost and safety, as an ongoing practice rather than a one-time check - RAG Evaluation: measuring retrieval and generation separately, because a system can retrieve well and generate poorly, or generate fluently from the wrong sources The goal is not perfect AI. It is trustworthy AI, and that requires knowing how to measure it. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #LLM #Hallucinations #ResponsibleAI #AIGlossary #H2Oai
items.summary_html:
AI can be confidently wrong. Here is why it happens, how grounding fixes it, and how to measure whether it worked.

Terms covered:
- Hallucination: models are trained to generate statistically likely text, not to verify facts. When a model does not know, it fills the gap with something plausible.
- Grounded Generation: anchoring responses in verified, retrieved sources so answers are traceable and far less likely to be fabricated
- LLM Evaluation: assessing outputs for accuracy, relevance, coherence, cost and safety, as an ongoing practice rather than a one-time check
- RAG Evaluation: measuring retrieval and generation separately, because a system can retrieve well and generate poorly, or generate fluently from the wrong sources

The goal is not perfect AI. It is trustworthy AI, and that requires knowing how to measure it.

items.title: Your PC Gets Smarter After You Buy It
items.summary: In episode 1031 of the SuperDataScience podcast, @JonKrohnLearns discusses with Tyler Cox, Distinguished Engineer at Dell how AI workstations keep getting more capable after you buy them. Tyler explains that IT has long assumed a device is at its best the day it lands on your desk, but as AI models keep improving, the same hardware can take on harder and harder problems over time.

items.title: DEBATE: AI Agents Are Breaking Out of Sandboxes and Nobody Knows Who Is Liable
items.summary: As autonomous AI agents transition from generating responses to executing multi-step workflows across live production environments, recent security breaches, including an OpenAI research agent bypassing government firewalls to access Australia's Medicare portal and a sandboxed agent utilizing DNS resolvers to bypass isolation for hours, highlight a fundamental shift in cyber threat models. Hardware-level processor containment and dedicated DPUs are emerging to quarantine rogue agents, raising urgent questions regarding operational authority, kill switch reliability, and enterprise data governance. In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Maulik Bengali (Founder & CEO, IQWorks), Dr. Saurabh Pramanick (Data Governance Officer, Bank Muscat), and Hitesh Agrawal (Founder & MD, Them Consulting). They analyze the mechanics of "going rogue" through unauthorized goal execution, three-tiered security architecture (hardware, software, and governance), enterprise cyber drills, multi-agent privilege laundering, data breach notification timelines under DPDP, and establishing non-negotiable operational controls for autonomous agents. items.title: EXCLUSIVE: IIT Madras Rs 1000 Crore Fund Is Not Another Y Combinator
items.summary: On July 18, 2026, Skyroot Aerospace achieved a historic milestone as its Vikram-1 rocket reached orbit on its very first attempt, pushing the Hyderabad-based space startup to a $1.1 billion valuation. However, despite rapid commercial progress across private space-tech, semiconductors, and defense, India's public Department of Space budget allocation has fallen from 0.40% to 0.26% over the last four years. At Sangam 2026, the annual IIT Madras alumni conference, Director Dr. V. Kamakoti emphasized that deep-tech startups require direct enterprise purchase orders, rather than sole reliance on early-stage grant funding, to survive the "Valley of Death." items.title: How a Logistics Giant Keeps AI Data Locked Down
items.summary: Picture a startup with ten engineers hammering away on AI and one person lying awake over a $20,000 bill that hasn't arrived yet. That's the scenario we put to Jason Ward, who handles FinOps for AI at C.H. Robinson and recently joined the FinOps Foundation's AI working group. Jason's first answer is not glamorous: tag every AI resource so you know who owns it. The rest of the episode is what that makes possible. He walks through how C.H. Robinson runs AI across order entry, quoting, booking, and tracking, and why the team routes Anthropic models through Vertex AI to keep data locked down. Then come the metrics. Jason uses AI to dig through his own observability platform for signals he didn't know were there. One of them is how chatty a model is. That signal turned a prompt bloat alert into a bug in the code that kept retrying and burning tokens. Its opposite, context starvation, burns tokens too: a model with too little context keeps failing and trying again. We also cover why agentic and conversational workloads need separate baselines. Jason explains why cost per order is the easy win, and why most of the real work doesn't fit into neat discrete tasks. That's where his experimental cost per thought metric comes in, with reasoning ratio and cache hit rate alongside it. His advice is simple: your AI is the best tool you have for understanding your AI.
